overall: The AG found the Wayland School Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law as alleged: individual member review of executive session minutes was permissible, and the open-session announcements were made. A supplemental subcommittee allegation was not reviewed.

allegations.summary: Review of executive session minutes occurred outside a noticed meeting, and no notice told the public of the plan to review them.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that review of executive session minutes for release be conducted in a noticed meeting.

allegations.summary: A quorum deliberated on release of executive session minutes outside a meeting when three members divided up the review.
allegations.key_passage: Mr. Harris’s speculation, without more, that the three reviewing Committee members deliberated outside of a meeting cannot serve as the basis of a finding of a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The committee did not announce in open session the outcome of its reviews of executive session minutes.
allegations.key_passage: Minutes of the July 19 and August 23 meeting reflect announcements in open session of the Committee’s determination regarding recently reviewed executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: The committee failed to discuss its procedure for periodic review of executive session minutes during an open meeting.
allegations.key_passage: there is nothing within the Open Meeting Law that requires that a public body outline its review procedure during a meeting; the Law only requires that a public body announce the outcome of the review.

allegations.summary: Supplement alleged a three-member subcommittee formed to review minutes deliberated on release; not raised in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: As this allegation was not raised in the complaint of August 17, we do not consider it here.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
